title: Training Note — Voluntary Contribution Availability across Employer UI Tax Account Classes
content:
Whether an account within the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts may make a voluntary contribution, how long after the rate notice mailing date it may be received, and whether it can be refunded are set by financing class.

| Financing class | Voluntary contribution allowed | Window after the rate notice mailing date (calendar days) | Refundable |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contributory — New Employer Standard Rate | No | 0 — not available | No |
| Contributory — New Employer Construction Rate | No | 0 — not available | No |
| Contributory — Experience-Rated Positive Reserve | Yes | 30 | No |
| Contributory — Experience-Rated Deficit Reserve | Yes | 30 | No |
| Contributory — Delinquent Reporting Assigned Rate | No | 0 — not available | No |
| Reimbursing — Nonprofit Organization | No | 0 — not available | No |
| Reimbursing — Governmental Entity | No | 0 — not available | No |

## Questions this table answers

**Which classes can make a voluntary contribution at all?** Only the two experience-rated reserve classes, Contributory — Experience-Rated Positive Reserve and Contributory — Experience-Rated Deficit Reserve. Every other class shows "No" and a window of 0, which means the option is not available.

**How long is the window where it exists?** 30 calendar days after the rate notice mailing date.

**Can a voluntary contribution ever be refunded?** No class allows it; the refundable column reads "No" for all seven classes.

**Hypothetical comparison.** An employer in Contributory — Experience-Rated Deficit Reserve and an employer in Contributory — Delinquent Reporting Assigned Rate each receive a rate notice on the same day. The first has a 30-day window open to it; the second has none, because its class does not allow voluntary contributions.
